prompt: Answer-isolated transfer: in a clean normal-user Ubuntu 24.04 or WSL 2 Ubuntu 24.04 environment, use only the supported lifecycle for the transfer case in book/labs/LES-0009-safe-local-workbench. Without reading another learner's work or seeking a model answer, classify every Git state across HEAD, index, working tree, untracked, and ignored boundaries; decide what evidence and work would require preservation in a real repository; predict selective recovery; recover through the supported interface; verify the modeled operation; and prove cleanup. Use no sudo, network, remote, real credential, employer data, production path, manual descriptor/root editing, force, reset --hard, clean, broad deletion, package installation, port, Docker, or background process.
deliverables: A sanitized safety card naming OS, kernel or WSL boundary, Bash and Git versions, effective UID, exact lesson scope, no-network/no-remote contract, changed resources, time box, abort conditions, supported recovery, and cleanup proof.
The clean baseline record followed by transfer status; a path-by-path table classifying HEAD, index, worktree, untracked, and ignored state without including placeholder-value content.

Ordinary and cached diff evidence with a three-version explanation wherever both status columns differ; each observation states what it proves, does not prove, and which concurrent-change limit applies.
A repository state diagram from shell and canonical root through working tree, index, object database, branch and conceptual remote boundary, labeling trust, ownership, mutation, and evidence points.
A written decision for each changed path: preserve, review, stage, unstage, restore, or remove in a real repository, with owner/intent evidence required before action.

A recovery prediction written before the supported recover command, including expected branch, HEAD, tracked bytes, clean status, remote count, fixture-local ignored/untracked absence, abort, and response to refusal.
Operation-verification and status evidence after recovery, explaining why fixture success does not prove production rollback, secret safety, remote policy, or learner mastery.
Exact guarded cleanup plus a following check showing absent state; no personal path, hostname, remote URL, credential-like value, employer identifier, or raw sensitive output may be submitted.

A production transfer to one unfamiliar setting (CI/CD, GitOps/Kubernetes, data pipeline, or private-cloud IaC) that maps commit, artifact/desired state, promotion, runtime, user outcome, credential handling, rollback compatibility, observability, capacity/cost, and collaboration policy.
A short later-recall record, completed without the lesson open, answering why MM needs two diffs, why ignore is not secret remediation, and why source rollback is not operational recovery.
evidenceRequirements: Begin with bash lab.sh check showing ready environment and absent state; use setup, run baseline, and exactly inject transfer. A second case requires guarded reset and is outside this submission.

Use only supported observe status|worktree|staged|ignored|history and status commands before recovery. Do not inspect or edit .git internals, descriptor, sentinel, lifecycle records, or fixture files directly.
Record the question and prediction before every mutating supported command. A post-hoc explanation does not satisfy prediction evidence.
Decode every porcelain state exactly. Untracked or ignored must never be equated with disposable or safe, and the placeholder content must not be printed in submitted evidence.
Show both ordinary and cached diff views and relate each to the correct source/destination boundary; identify what neither view contains.
State which work a real incident would preserve and which human or policy authority would be needed. The fixture recover command is allowed only after this decision is written.

Use supported recover and verify-operation. Verify branch, HEAD, tracked baseline bytes, clean status, zero remotes, fixture-local temporary-file absence, and lifecycle status; distinguish restoration from root-cause or mastery claims.

Run supported cleanup and a following check. If any guard refuses because of a changed path, link, owner, top-level entry, descriptor, or lifecycle condition, stop and preserve the diagnostic rather than bypassing it.

The production transfer must preserve the separation between repository ref, build/render output, immutable artifact or desired state, promotion/reconciliation, runtime, durable external effects, and user verification.

Submit original sanitized reasoning and disclose assistance. Reading guided answers is allowed only before starting a fresh transfer attempt; obtaining transfer-specific answers or inspecting fixture implementation to extract them invalidates independence.

rubric.observableEvidence: Uses clean normal-user bounded lifecycle, records predictions and refusals, protects sensitive context, and proves exact cleanup without unsupported mutation.
Correctly maps every path and both status columns across HEAD, index, worktree, untracked, and ignored boundaries using both diffs.
Separates observation from interpretation, states proof limits, and names preservation/authority requirements before recovery.
Predicts selective recovery, uses the supported path, verifies branch/HEAD/content/status/remotes/temp state, and avoids overclaiming.
Maps source through consumer outcome with secrets, collaboration, rollback, external state, reliability, observability, capacity/cost, limitations, and later recall.
